description: Encrypt text with real AES-256-GCM using a password-derived key (PBKDF2), fully in your browser.

faqs.a: Yes. It uses WebCrypto PBKDF2 with 100,000 SHA-256 iterations and a random salt to derive an AES-256-GCM key — the same building blocks used by professional tools. The main weakness is a short, guessable password.
Each encryption uses a fresh random salt and IV, so encrypting the same text twice produces different output. Both are needed to decrypt.
faqs.q: Why does encrypting the same text give different output?

faqs.a: No. Decryption fails and you get a clear error. There is no password recovery — keep your password safe.
faqs.q: What if I forget the password?

faqs.a: The encrypted output is self-contained: salt, IV and ciphertext packed into one Base64 string, so it decrypts on any device with the password.
faqs.q: Can I decrypt on another device?

howto: Enter a strong password (you will need it to decrypt).
Paste your text (or the encrypted Base64 string) and click the button.
Copy the result — the output packs salt, IV and ciphertext into one string.
title: AES Text Encryptor
